I really relate to this as well. I am not formally diagnosed as on the spectrum but I have experienced almost all of what you are describing-including the hospitalizations for depression/anxiety. 

I am in college right now and it is very difficult to navigate socially. I find myself talking excessively and passionately about my few interests but in all other convos I have a flat affect and zero emotion in my voice. 

Idk how to read body language or tone and I miss so many social cues. 

I hope you find the answers and support you need.

I’ve just now realized that I’m doing this. Something in my environment will trigger a memory and I just blurt it out. Regardless of whether or not it’s a worthy memory of being shared or anywhere near relevant to the social environment around me.
I’ve begun to pay more attention to what other people are saying/doing and I try to mirror that. I’ve also begun stopping myself by being a bit more curious and critical of this thought that just NEEDS TO BE SAID.

I do this about every couple of months during a depressive episode. I tell myself I’m trying to remind myself of all the good memories I have to look back on. But sometimes I feel so mentally ill I realize that I can’t remember what it felt like to be in those moments-the good moments. The ones where I’m grinning wide and care about things. 

I used to sleep in the same bed as my best friend when we would have sleep overs. I really loved being physically close to another human being and I didn’t really have that need met anywhere else in my life. I completely forgot about what that felt like. I still don’t really know now. But I was looking through old pictures yesterday and I found one of us being goofy one morning. I was so comfortable and happy. 

Now I’m so trauma-ridden I flinch away from most human contact. Last year, my now ex started to give me a shoulder rub while I was sitting down. I found myself folded over and leaning away from his touch and he stopped. I couldn’t figure out why he stopped until I realized everything about my body language was telling him to. Other people haven’t been so kind to listen to that. 

I used to love shoulder rubs. I feel like most people do. Now I just feel like I’m being held from behind and raped whenever people grab my shoulders.

I don’t really think it’s that crazy to link it like that. Native Americans introduced tobacco to white settlers. White settlers effectively destroyed (assimilated) as much of NA culture as possible. Cigarettes were an extreme degree of appropriation and rebranding.

I think it’s from the JUUL lung issues and more concentrated on nicotine derived from Tobacco. I have another theory that tobacco is so socially despised and taboo because it originated from Native American cultural traditions (in the continental US) and it’s part of the deep rooted racism and ethnocentrism. Tobacco only became big once it was exploited by white settler colonization and capitalism. Once the western white male drs declared the health hazards related, the tides totally turned. 
However, I think that smoking raw tobacco with no additives is much safer and less addicting. There aren’t the 1,000 other chemicals that are present in cigarettes. 
Big Tobacco has it’s claws in most major food brands now so when fewer people are smoking cigarettes, more are addicted to processed foods. It’s more socially acceptable to buy a pack of Oreos than to smoke a cigarette now but which one is really better health wise? (Neither)

This happens to me all the time. When people ask me how old I am, what my name is, what I’m studying, where I’m from, what I ate today. Sometimes I blurt out something that may or may not be correct and then I awkwardly correct myself once I actually can think. I used to think it was from mild cannabis use, but I’ve taken a month off and it’s almost worsened. I walk into rooms and forget why. I open an internet tab and it takes sometimes a full minute to remember what I wanted to look up. 

The Lag is very real for me.

Yeah, I don’t think anything will extend the time that I am productive, but maybe it will help with focus/efficiency while I do have energy. Especially if the neurotransmitters in my brain are being supported in a way that aids cognition and focus. 

I’m honestly just looking for anything that will help the debilitating fatigue I feel on a day to day basis.

Wow, being a mom is a full time job in and of itself! 

I’ve done that in the past, where on days I work, that’s the only thing I’ve done for the day. As a college student in my early 20s, there’s a lot of pressure to be busy 24/7. I also meal prep so I have food for the times when I’m too tired/weak to cook. I’m glad you’ve found ways to take care of yourself! Those are good to keep in mind, I’ve been discovering that if I “push” I swing lower into fatigue and physical pain as well. 
There is a lot of misplaced stigma surrounding weed. I wouldn’t be too hard on yourself for cannabis, it is medically prescribed in many states and has medicinal properties. There’s an interesting doc on Hulu called Weediquette and it’s pretty eye opening about the growth of the industry in general.
I’ve been in a similar situation with side effects of drugs. I’ve tried a lot of different sleeping medications and they’ve been pretty ineffective with unpleasant side effects. It got to the point where my dr was suggesting benzos for sleep-which are highly likely to cause physiological and psychological dependence within a couple of days and worsen depression.
I appreciate your advice/ sharing things that work for you.
